rāhulovādasutta:
[Rāhulovāda+sutta]  CL=9 (a) Cūḷarāhulovāda Sutta:
This sutta presents the Buddha"s instructions to his son Rāhula before he had completed even one rainy season as a monk. It outlines fifteen qualities that mature one for arahantship, aiming to help Rāhula realize the fruit of arahantship.
(b) Rāhulovāda Sutta or Rāhula Sutta:
This discourse shows the Buddha"s continuous guidance to his son Rāhula. It teaches how to:
- Eliminate craving for the four requisites
- Abandon attachment to the five sensual pleasures
- Recognize the importance of noble friends as reliable supports
(c) Ambalatthika Rāhulovāda Sutta:
This sutta records the Buddha"s advice to seven-year-old novice Rāhula on the importance of truthfulness. Knowing that young people often enjoy speaking untruthfully, the Buddha uses four similes of a water pot, two similes of an elephant, and four similes of a mirror to illustrate the importance of avoiding false speech.
For further information, also refer to the Rāhula Saṃyutta.
